title: docs: add a rule cookbook with end-to-end detection examples
problem: Contributors have a template but no worked examples showing the judgment calls behind a good detector.
why: The quality of new detectors depends on understanding evidence and false-positive trade-offs.
scope: Add `docs/rules/cookbook.md` with three annotated examples (one heuristic, one structural, one metadata-based).
guidance: Reference the real fixtures used by existing rules.
acceptance: Cookbook linked from the writing-rules guide

title: docs: explain the detection methodology and its limits
problem: Users may over-trust findings without understanding that detection is syntactic and heuristic.
why: Honest methodology documentation prevents misuse and sets expectations.
scope: Add `docs/analysis-methodology.md` covering what static analysis can and cannot prove, and how confidence is assigned.
guidance: Use concrete examples from SS-001 and SS-006.
acceptance: Linked from README and rules docs
security: Explicitly state the scanner is not an audit replacement.

title: docs: add a FAQ
problem: Recurring questions about false positives, CI gating, and supported versions are scattered.
why: A FAQ reduces support burden and improves onboarding.
scope: Add `docs/faq.md` covering at least ten real questions.
guidance: Link answers to the detailed docs.
acceptance: FAQ linked from the documentation index

title: docs(adr): record the confidence and severity methodology
problem: The rules for assigning severity and confidence live only in the rules README.
why: An ADR captures the rationale and makes future changes deliberate.

title: ci(docs): run the documentation link checker in CI
problem: `tools/check_docs.py` exists but is not run automatically, so broken links can be merged.
scope: Add a CI job invoking the documentation link checker.
guidance: Use the system Python available on ubuntu-latest.
security: The checker is offline and read-only.
